Usage: mail-find fetch (--attachment=NAME | --all) <id> [flags]

Download a message's attachments and print where each landed.

Writes the chosen attachments to disk: into --out, or else the message's
own directory under $XDG_STATE_HOME/mailkit/attachments/ (by default
~/.local/state/mailkit/attachments/), never the working directory. Names
are made safe for the disk, and two files that would collide get -2, -3.
Only stored parts have bytes; for a cloud link or an embedded message fetch
says there is nothing to download, and attachments shows what each holds.

A downloaded file is a path, not yet read: open it to see what it says.

Arguments:
  <id>                     The message's id.

Flags:
      --attachment=NAME    Download the attachment with this name or handle. A name two attachments
                           share needs its handle (repeatable).
      --all                Download every attachment that has bytes in the message.
      --out=DIR            Directory to write into, in place of the message's state directory.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help               Show context-sensitive help.
      --account=ACCOUNT    Which account's mailbox to read. An id from one account means nothing in
                           the other (default: gmail; one of: gmail, outlook).
      --text               Print the human form instead of one JSON document.

Constraints:
  Exactly one of --attachment, --all.

Examples:
  mail-find fetch 1a01c98dd4e47691 --attachment report.pdf --attachment data.csv
  mail-find fetch 1a01c98dd4e47691 --all --out ./downloads

JSON:
  saved, each file with name (as the mail gave it), path and size.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
